outgoing.name: Astrology
outgoing.excerpt: In the astrology of the Middle Ages, Sirius was a Behenian fixed star, associated with beryl and juniper.

outgoing.name: Carl Sagan
outgoing.excerpt: This work has been challenged by astronomer Carl Sagan, among others, as based on selective evidence.

outgoing.name: Chinese language
outgoing.excerpt: In Chinese the star is known as 天狼星 (Tiānláng xīng literally, “heavenly wolf star”).

outgoing.name: Greek mythology
outgoing.excerpt: In Greek mythology, Orion's dog became Sirius.

outgoing.name: Middle Ages
outgoing.excerpt: In the astrology of the Middle Ages, Sirius was a Behenian fixed star, associated with beryl and juniper.

outgoing.name: Popular culture
outgoing.excerpt: Being the brightest star in the night sky, Sirius is often mentioned in science fiction and other popular culture as well.

outgoing.name: Rome
outgoing.excerpt: Sirius was worshipped as Sothis in the valley of the Nile long before Rome was founded.

outgoing.name: Sanskrit
outgoing.excerpt: In Sanskrit, it is known as Mrgavyadha ("deer hunter") or Lubdhaka ("hunter").
